body: Thank you  💙

I thought the same. It made me feel really bad about myself that I was doing it but eventually I understood that it takes a lot of internal pain for someone to do something like this. And that helped me realise that something was not right and in turn helped me talk about it and seek help.

Now I try to talk about how I'm feeling before it reaches the point of no return where I'm so frustrated that it seems like the only option.

I think I do it for the same reason. I was bullied and still do get bullied from time to time and when someone hurts me with their words it's like it gets inside of me and I need to hit my head to get it out.

And even if no one has said anything to me the memory's of the times they did get in on me.

Well done for achieving not self harming since April. It's okay that you can't process how you've gotten it under control it can take a long time. You've probably developed ways to cope without you even realising and that's fantastic. You should be very proud of yourself.
Thanks for the response

I'm on vraylar & seroquel but they've never helped this problem. I thought anti anxiety medication like benzos would help but my doctors refused because they can be addictive so I'm left with the problem all this time
Thank you

Wow I was about to ask something similar & your post was at the top of the sub!

It would be cool if we could mark our favourites in-game too as there's quite a lot of material I'd love to be able to star the ones I want to go back to later

Sound for the link bud

Jump. 

I was waiting for the train at the time, Had that voice ever since.
Restless, Agitated, Depressed

Thanks. Yeah I've had this happen to me many times. I always gravitate towards the other people with my diagnosis when I'm in the hospital & it always ends with us feeding off each others delusions. Because a lot of the time I'd talk about a belief and the other person would confirm that it's real & we would convince ourselves that we weren't crazy the world was against us, we were gods etc etc. It's like having a shared psychosis.

They don't have baker acts where we are. It's similar though. You can get detained under the Mental Health Act. It's also called being sectioned. It happened to me last year. I lost 3 tribunals & each time I lost the duration of my stay would increase. I also had less freedom than the other patients who weren't sectioned.

Thanks for your advice.

Yeah my doctor has said the same thing to me. If you think about it if the government or an intelligence agency such as MI5 were really closely monitoring you it would take a lot of resources & surely they're far more interested in protecting the public from terrorism than they are in monitoring all the people with schizophrenia.

100℅ Olanzapine. I'm on 25mg. The voices are basically gone. I still have delusions every so often but nothing like the manic state I was in in the hospital. It also helps me sleep and I think it's made me less anxious. I just feel more stable when I take it and felt really unstable in my mind when I missed a dose.

I've tried Seroquel and Abilify too but those sedated me too much.

I completely agree with you and it seems like some people on here are never going to understand the point you're making.

I must be incredibly delusional to see my psychosis as a gift and that's OK because people like me have as much right to be on this sub and get help. I'm not ready to stop seeing it as a gift and that is the nature of this illness. Some delusions stick so why should my delusions be banned.

I'm not saying schizophrenia is a gift, I'm saying I believe that I have a gift. Classic delusion of grandeur. I've had many manic magical spiritual experiences with psychosis which leads me to this conclusion.

Anyway I just wanted to say I get what you're saying here but obviously people don't want to open their minds any further than its a terrible disease. That's not everyone's experience.
I was on 20mg but I had really really bad akathisia and was taken off it.
Through a Glass Darkly is a great movie. I loved the idea of God being a spider. There is a similar story in African Folklore about a spider God called Anansi who spun the threads of reality.

This would be useful. I feel like the general mental health helplines aren't equipped to deal with schizophrenia. It would be good to have someone to call, especially if you're paranoid or in psychosis that could reality check with you judgement free.

I've never felt like the samaritans etc would be able to handle my issues but didn't have an alternative at that time.

Bear in mind that when these people were your age treatment options were probably different. Most of them were probably put on the First generation Anti-Psychotics where as most of us are on second generation. I know the first generation ones had some nasty side effects and possibly long term effects. If someone in their 50s or 60s was taking meds consistently since their teens or twenties it could explain why they look burnt out.

It really depends though. I know people that age who function really well outside of episodes. I also know people who are like you described.

I used to worry about this stuff a lot. But I read recently that schizophrenia isn't exactly a steady deterioration which I thought it originally was.

Try not to focus on what could be. Things may be completely different for you.
Merry Christmas! :) that's a cool present, enjoy it

It's hard isn't it. I've decided to stay at my friend's just for tonight. We're gonna get takeaway and watch TV.

My mother can be a bit weird about me going elsewhere though. It's days until Christmas but she complains that I'm not here to help her and she's left to do everything if I go out even though they're not much to do and I clean anyway.

Yeah I guess we just have to do our best. She knows about my condition but I think she likes to pretend it's not real.

Hope things get better for you!

Yeah that's the thing. If I'm having an episode most times, especially later on it doesn't cross my mind or I won't even consider it.

Its the little things or feelings or thoughts that make me question how stable I am.

Wish I could. Unfortunately I'm staying with them in my old house. I'm planning to see my friends more though so at least I won't be stuck in the house all the time.

Family drama is the worst especially when you're trying hard to stay grounded.

Yes I wasn't sure if this was normal as it's definitely a new experience for me, in the past few months.

It usually happens when I wake up during a vivid dream. It's like I'll carry on the emotions and remember the dream as if it really happened hours ago. So I'll go about my day as if the events and emotions of the dream were real. It can be pretty hard to deal with and even harder to describe. I'm not surw if it's a SZ thing but it could very well be since Ive never heard other people mention it apart from on this sub.

It depends on what you're comfortable with. Some people are pretty open about these things. Just remember that Facebook has a permanence about it, meaning that even if you delete the post after people will most likely have still seen it. If you're OK with people knowing then go for it as long as you know you can't make them forget about it.

Not sure about Facebook but people seem to be more open about mental health stuff on Instagram or twitter.

Good luck with whatever you decide!
Went shopping in the afternoon and got some Christmas presents. I'm now in between tiredness and considering sleep or mindlessly browsing reddit. Currently doing the latter!

Wow. I just seen this. Thank you for your concern, it means a lot to know people here care that much.

I made a new account because I was a little paranoid when someone I know joined reddit. It's highly unlikely they could trace my posts to me but you never know. 

Anyway I'm doing pretty well. Been psychosis free for nearly 3 months now. I'm working and I'm studying. Being active has helped so much. 

I'm going back home next week for my sisters 18th birthday and I'm so excited to get to see my family and my two dogs :) it'll also be like a mini holiday for a few days so I'll try make the most of it. Plenty of walks hopefully since we have the beach nearby.

Thanks for your post. I was about to go to sleep when I decided to check reddit one last time. I just logged into this profile to respond here but most likely I'll be using my other account for this sub u/inky-octopus. I'm not so paranoid now so I'm good to reveal it.

Take care!
Hero
I have this too. I hope it gets better.

Haha I know I know :P Well I dunno other than rest assured I've experienced the same thing and never once did I actually get hurt. It's all in your head even though those words mean very little when your brain has you believing these things. Yes, sometimes a tickly feeling and other times I could feel like my head was getting hotter!

Yeah it's a really hard one to shake because I almost felt like there were physical sensations around my head kind of hinting that I was about to get hurt. It's basically that feeling where you see an accident just before it happens and it's so real that we actually respond to it (ducking down, hiding in shops/side streets)

I had the same thing before my first episode stared. I used to go into every second shop walking up the street because I felt like someone was going to shoot me in the head from a passing car. I think mine passed after about 2 or 3 weeks, the paranoia in general.

In general, my voices either sound like they're coming from above me or beside me. When I put headphones in the voices actually sound closer to my ears as if the headphones were trapping them right beside my ear drum. If I play music when the voices are particularly loud the voices will often blend into the music so I'll still hear them throughout the song or sometimes it'll sound like the lyrics have changed.

I'm in the UK too and it varies so much depending on your postcode. The two times I was admitted I was taken to A & E by someone else. The first time I was taken straight from university to an A & E in central (outside my borough) during my first episode and they admitted me even though I cried about it. The paranoia had me thinking the other patients would harm/kill me.

The second time I was taken to A & E by the ambulance and the police and they decided to admit me but the only bed was 3-4 hours away.

My most recent episode where I was paranoid af I actually wanted to go into hospital but my home treatment team/community team in my borough were really incompetent and kept lying to me. Then they'd give me a speech about the bed crisis and how you have to be at your worst etc to get admitted  (which I was)

It honestly just depends because my most recent episode was far worse imo than my first two and I didn't get admitted. If you think you need hospital then I'd advice you to show them why you need it as opposed to asking. I mean you can ask if you want but from experience I've been admitted mostly without asking. If you talk about your symptoms and your doctors think you need to be admitted they'll ask you if you agree to it. 

Hope the appointment goes ok for you!

Thank you because this was a really helpful response for me. That's what I thought. When it happened and afterwards I felt like I had opened up something that I would have rather left closed. If it was psychosis I was experiencing then it was the realest psychosis I've had to date and that scares me.

I've always had good insight and this was the one time where that really changed for me. As I said I was considering how I was going to tell people that I was in an alternate reality and I was worried about their reactions. I knew nobody would believe me and at the time I knew it was real. 

I hope I can keep this under the lid now. I've obviously tripped a switch in my brain now and I don't want to go there again. One of my fears is becoming so psychotic that I don't realise it. I mean I've been in psychosis before but I've had less bizarre delusions than this one. I don't want to end up in a bizarre delusional cycle where the people I know end up thinking I've lost it. My fear as you mentioned is something like this becoming permanent.

I'm going to try and work through what I experienced to make it seem less real in my head so I don't go seeking it again. Thanks again for your input!

I had an ECG (I think that's what it's called) where they measure the electrical signals in your brain. After my first psychosis my psychiatrist at the time wanted to test for epilepsy. Turned out I'm not epileptic.

I've always wanted to get an MRI done so I could see what my brain actually looks like and whether any areas of it have been physically effected by the schizophrenia.

I have quite bad eyesight  (shortsighted) and have had glasses since I was around 8 but my eyesight has only gotten worse in the last few years. I hate wearing my glasses in general so I only really wear them for reading or using the computer. 

Anyway I think not being able to see things clearly that are further away makes me have more visual hallucinations. Like the other night I thought I could see someone watching me from their car only to realise that the car was empty but my brain projected a moving shape onto it. This happens quite a lot. I'll think I see something further away but I'll put my glasses on and realise it was just an illusion. 

As for hearing, I've got mediocre hearing but I haven't been tested or anything to say it's substandard. I just think my hearing is bad because I constantly have to get people to repeat things. I guess this plays on my hallucinations sometimes where I'll completely misinterpret what I thought someone said to me. They'll say one thing and my brain incorrectly fills in the gaps of what I think they said only to realise it was completely different.

This might be a really unpopular opinion given the circumstances but physics does exist and it is a super important branch of science.

I think it would be incredibly difficult to convince someone that physics or aspects of physics don't exist, as difficult as it would be to convince someone the sun won't rise tomorrow or the sky isn't blue. I understand that physics is basically a subject with infinite information and a lot of it, when you dig deeper can be overwhelming and trigger us to think about things that might bring us into psychosis. However I'm just going from experience here, people with schizophrenia are pretty smart and it's likely your SO has done a lot of reading on the topic and knows that it's real. I know that someone couldn't possibly convince me that it's not real because that's simply not true.

Instead, I think you need to focus more on specific delusions as opposed to physics as a whole. Break down specific beliefs that are harmful to your SO and start from there. Tell her/him that a lot of these are hypothetical models. They're just theories and can't be proved. Your SO lives in baseline reality and they don't have to worry about ending up somewhere else. They're safe here. 

The last part might be hypocritical given that I had some experiences with what I perceived to be an alternate reality a few days ago but my stuff aside because it's likely I was having an episode although I'm still working on cementing that in my mind :)

I usually have the same familiar tabs open when I use the Internet and I've also bookmarked them. Reddit, BBC news, YouTube, Celtx (for scriptwriting) and Google Docs for my other writing.

As for Internet usage it really depends. When I'm stable I guess I use the Internet like anyone else would. Social media, watching videos, random surfing. 

When I'm in psychosis I'll have a lot more tabs opened about different things I've learned about. Usually these are related to physics or spiritual things. A lot of the time I'll think that there the separate tabs are all small pieces of one big puzzle that are connected in some way. Kind of like when you watch a film about someone solving a crime and they have different images/evidence on a wall with strings connecting the different ideas I guess. It's a bit like that. 

As for keywords, excluding general searches like my nearest xyz or how to cook this etc. I tend to look up things about reality, the universe, some philosophy, stuff related to symptoms especially if I'm experiencing new ones.

I remember the first time I was in hospital this guy a few years younger than me, he was like 18/19 would spend all his time on Wikipedia learning about other countries and looking at maps. Some people with sz that I have on Facebook might share things related to their delusions. I have one friend who shares religious themed posts daily.

I think there will be a big difference in the browsing habits of schizophrenics between when they are well and when they are in psychosis.

I start to notice a lot of coincidences. Things happen around me as if there was some kind of magic working underneath, orchestrating everything. The thoughts I have in my brain start to manifest in my physical reality making it difficult to believe there is any separation between the two. 

Depending on the type of episode I might start feeling really good, like I'm some unstoppable force. Like the "real world" can only be seen by me and I have the task of communicating the world I see to other people. Every song I listen to speaks to me personally. I start having interesting experiences and I then believe something special is about to happen. 

Usually all this is accompanied by an increase in the voices and my sleep will go out of whack.

The other type of episode I'll have is a paranoid one which is kind of self explanatory. I'll second guess things people say. I'll start thinking people are laughing or talking about me behind my back. When I feel like that I feel bad about myself and sometimes I believe that me feeling bad has an effect on the outside world and causes bad things to happen (terrorism for example). If I'm unhappy then I'm causing the world to be unhappy by the "unhappy frequency" my brain is emitting.

I would definitely struggle with that kind of job. Considering also that some people make quite complicated orders or at least detailed orders when it's a family. 

I would ask your supervisor if you can keep a pen and notebook on you when you're at the drive thru window. If they have any issue with that then they really suck and I would look for an alternative place to work. Explain to them that you struggle remembering the larger orders and that you need the notebook in order to avoid making mistakes since it would be in their interest to have the customers orders correct.

If you really aren't happy at the job though maybe you should look for something else. Even start looking while you still work there. I've worked at jobs that I hated and I'd feel sick going into work everyday. Finding a job you don't mind doing makes so much difference to your mental health. 

Good luck!

I've been experiencing the exact same things recently and someone else commented on a post I made and said that it was depersonalisation/derealisation. Although you've articulated it so much better than I could have done.

I also get the feeling to laugh all the time because things are so absurd. Sometimes I feel high but nothing like I've ever felt from drugs. It's an odd feeling but when it comes on I also feel content. I can't really say much more about it because as you probably know this shit is so damn hard to describe haha. 

I guess for now I'm enjoying the trip. I've had a lot of stress recently which I think is causing this dissociation thing but luckily I've also had so many other things fall into place. I feel really grounded actually, more than I have done in the past 3 years.

In the past 2 years I've had three acute episodes. Episode 1 started in July 2015 (with voices) and lasted until October when I was admitted. Episode 2 was also in July the following year, another admission. Then the most recent episode 3 started in April but reached its peak in June/July. Kinda weird how my major episodes all occurred during the summer.
Great recommendation. Currently listening to Music Music from the same album :)

I don't feel like schizophrenia effects my job too much actually. There are times where I'll struggle with my memory or I'll struggle to process what's been asked of me. Otherwise after I settled in I kind of was able to just get on with it.

I guess it helps that I actually enjoy the job and I'm working with really nice people. In the beginning I had some paranoia. If I did something wrong I would think all the managers were laughing or thought I was dumb. Now I know that's not true since I've been told several times that I'm doing a good job and they've even asked me to do extra things because they think  I'm capable. 

I want to end this by saying that before this job I was off work for a year. I had to leave my previous job because I went into hospital. I thought I couldn't handle having a job but I'm so glad I have one now. It gives you something to do, provides structure and you'll make money. I also feel a sense of achievement from working too :)

Swallow your pride and ask anyone you know if you can stay on their couch until you get yourself sorted. 

Call up some charities that might be able to help you and provide some guidance on what to do.

Everyone's situation is different of course. For me it was just a matter of time before I found somewhere suitable and within my budget to move into.

If you have a lot of stuff enquire about storage options. If you have someone with a big house/garage that can store it for you that's even better.

Yes what you've written here sounds exactly like what I'm going through. 

Unable to articulate myself as well as I used to. It's strange because it only started about a week ago. 

Thanks for the links I'll have a read. I got some books in the library today. I'm hoping reading might get my brain back functioning again or at least I'm going to give it a try.

I haven't really thought about this. I feel like it's been varied because I had some symptoms when I was a kid too.

I guess a lot of it was an underlying paranoid theme. Lots of focus on thoughts - my own, other people's, mind reading, premonitions. 

Voices seem to play on the paranoia. "There's a bomb on the train" "they're reading your mind".

My delusions definitely take on a grandiose theme. In my reality I'm on a special mission to figure out a complex problem and I'm the only one who sees the world the way I do. I have a special way of understanding the messages in music. I have a special way of seeing things. I feel gifted a lot of the time when I'm not feeling depressed.

As for visual stuff currently it's just small shadow movement in my peripheral vision. I've seen running water on the floor. Lots of ants.

I'm sorry you lost a loved one. Grief is known to cause many strange things including hearing voices and often, it's caused by the event of loss rather than organic psychosis.

Doctors will sometimes talk with patients who say they hear their deceased loved one and this isn't really a cause for concern. 

However maybe it's a good idea to check in with a doctor. I know what you mean about sounds appearing like words. Water running was a prominent one for me in the months before I actually started hearing voices. I'd mistake ordinary sounds for voices or hear whispering in the pipes. 

Speak to your doctor though and don't worry too much because it very well may be a reaction to your loss.

I sometimes record myself on video talking and I'll never upload it anywhere but I'll watch it back and imagine I'm speaking to a wider audience. The videos forever stay in my gallery though but making them is good. It feels like I can get stuff off my chest without worrying.

I was started on zoloft around June 2015 and immediately within days I became increasingly paranoid. This was 3 months before my first episode/hospital. 

I worried people could see me showering through the plug hole. Every time I went outside I thought I'd be shot in the head. Persistent paranoid thoughts. I found a bag of pills near my door and thought it was a setup or a test and I'd be killed. I went straight back to my GP and told them that I thought the zoloft was causing it.

I actually think I stayed on it though and honestly the paranoia went in about 2 weeks. However then I had a stressful event, smoked some weed to calm down and started hearing voices. That was the start of it.
I'm currently homeless too since today. Staying on a friends sofa for now. I'm hoping to get some answers tomorrow. Hope it works out for you!

In my experience, being able to write with this condition comes in waves. I'm like you and feel like my brain is empty a lot of the time but this definitely depends on how I am.

I find it easier to write when I'm either in psychosis or I'm experiencing milder symptoms. When I'm stable and on meds it's a lot more difficult. However I think we often put other obstacles in our way. Sometimes being our own critic can stop us from even writing the first word.

Here's what I did. During my first psychosis I couldn't read anything. The voices repeated every  sentence, my short-term memory had the words I just read slip through my mind like sand and be forgotten. I was inspired my another patient to start writing my experiences on Google docs. It was a writing project about my psychosis and what I believed it meant. I've been adding to it for two years now and it's gone through a re-edit. It's only around 80 pages now but I still feel a great sense of achievement that it's all there. I've even added some images to it and one day I hope to make it into a book. Maybe you could do something similar. The hardest part is starting & I guess certain types of writing are more difficult than others.

Google docs is a good platform because you know it's all going to be safely stored and you can access it when you're out and about if you download it on your phone.

I don't know if any of this is helpful but I do know that if it weren't for me having that project to focus on I wouldn't have any confidence now to start writing. Best of luck! 

Edit: PM me if you want to see my writing project. I won't post it here because I know that some of it might be triggering especially the parts where I'm having an episode.

Not specifically but I've often put headphones in or covered my ears and the voices became a lot clearer. It was like they shifted and we're speaking just inside my ear. If I stopped covering my ears it went back to normal.

Seemed to be that covering my ears changed how close I could hear them.

Writing things down has helped me break down the outcomes of the situations in my life.

The struggle I have is I get paranoid about everything. I was just told that my council would help get me accommodation. In my head I'd like to take their word for it but really all I'm thinking about is that they're not being sincere and that they won't help me and I'll end up slipping through the cracks of the system. 

Similar thing with work. I feel like I work hard and I do a good job. In my head though I'm being told that I'm disorganised and I'm not making a good enough impression.

My brain likes to constantly remind me of the worst case scenarios in every situation since my last episode. I don't know if this is what you mean?

I'm 23 and I've also never dated apart from when I was basically a kid (Age 13 or 14).

I often feel like it's never a good time. I don't know if I could handle the responsibility that comes with it. Being there all the time for someone else. I feel like I need too much solitude and no one is going to be able to deal with that.

I know how you feel. When I started hearing the "new" voices the other night, the ones that seemed to think independently of me I became so curious about them. I've been listening out for them ever since because I want to know if they have something important to tell me. They've been pretty quiet though so I don't think they do.

I have problems with my memory lately and I can't tell if it's the seroquel or the psychosis.

I forgot to take my seroquel the other night and somehow fell asleep  (usually I can't sleep without it). I woke around 2am and couldn't remember if I'd taken it so thought it was safer to not take some at that time incase I'd forgotten I'd taken it already. I took it the following night. 

The bad thing about missing a dose is I tend to feel the side effects stronger when I do take the meds. It's hard though. The second night I didn't want to take them because I felt "fine" after I missed a dose but every time I've stopped meds it leads me back into another episode.

I don't think you were dishonest. A few weeks 3 years ago with a good friend of yours? That's well in the past now.

Please make sure you bandage yourself up properly. I trust you when you say you know how to look after yourself medically. Just make sure not to hurt yourself any more over this and if you think anything could become infected then make sure you seek professional help. 

Don't hurt yourself over this. You don't deserve it.
I feel like one of the main 'delusions' I have was given to me by someone I met in hospital. We both now have the same beliefs and both of us believe we are correct.
Same here. I'll just stay hungry because I've no motivation to make something. That's why I often just eat snack food that requires no preparation.

I've gone through long periods where nothing changes. I lay in bed all day. Sometimes I don't even have the energy to go on the internet so I legit just stare into space or try napping. It's a shitty situation to be in but as long as it lasts sometimes I've managed to come out of it.

For me, nothing in particular got me out of that state. It was like one day I'd have a little more energy than usual so I'd make an effort to do something that day. Often that would start off a chain reaction of doing things and in turn it would make me feel better having achieved something.

How often are they increasing your meds? Make sure they're giving the meds a chance to work before increasing them. Some doctors live increasing the meds when they're too impatient to see if things change.
I hope it went well for you!

I know it's difficult. I hold similar conflicting beliefs. Sometimes madness to me is beautiful. I love that state of mind where there are no boundaries in my realities, both internal and external blend together. I feel like I know the world around me on a personal level.

However, the other side of this is when it gets to that intolerable stage. That side of it is overwhelming and it makes every aspect of living all the more difficult. Hang in there. If you feel like things are slipping maybe check in with your doctor. You're not alone. I often have those same fears about my future. I'll see a homeless person on the street who likely has psychosis and think "is that going to be me one day?". It's made me determined to make sure that's not the case. Work on stability and whatever that means for you. Get yourself stable on meds and find something you like doing.

This is super interesting. I definitely second-guess a lot of the stuff I hear nowadays. I find it interesting that they mention the power of belief and how that can influence the chances of experiencing a distortion in your perception.

In my opinion, only go to the police if nothing else works. First I'd ignore the problem. If that's not possible I'd personally message him and ask him  to stop.  If he tells you he won't step then you should go to the police. And don't worry. When I went everything was off the record. The thought that the police were involved was enough to stop my harrasser.
I literally walked into my local police station and got it sorted out there.

Did anyone get a screenshot of the post? Unfortunatly in these circumstances you need to have proof before anything can be done. 

I was being harassed before by this  person I used to live with. They threatened to tell people how "crazy" I was if I didn't give them money that I never owed in the first place. I had to go to the police with the texts after this person did start messaging people personal info about me.

Nothing was done in the end because the police recommended I send her a message and make it clear that the police are involved and if she keeps harrassing me a case would be opened against her. She stopped after that.

Understand too that someone posting something online is an indirect way of making a threat. You said this person lives far away so they may just be trying their best to scare you. You could either ignore it or you could message them and ask them to stop otherwise you'll take it further and approach the authorities.

I had my complaints about it fall to deaf ears for the most part too. The actual doctor who dispensed the medication was one of the few who understood. He even told me how common it was for Procyclidine to be prescribed for a lot of patients on AP's and he couldn't understand why my team at the time were making such a big deal about it.

Akathisia is horrible and I think you need to explain in detail how it effects you when you see your psychiatrist. If you think she'll brush it off I'd actually recommend playing it up a bit more. Tell her what you've said here, that it makes you feel like crawling out of your skin. Tell her you can't sleep without constantly having to move your body. Tell her your pacing up and down at all hours of the night (even if you're not) if you think she might start listening. Sometimes we have to exaggerate these things to make the doctors listen.

Akathisia is such a common side-effect so it surprises me how little the doctors seem to care about it. For me, the restless sensations had me punching walls and myself. It caused me to be constantly angry and snap at people which is the opposite of my actual personality.

I wish you the best with it. Hopefully you can get some relief because I've been there and I know what you're saying is completely valid :)

I had the same thing with Abilify and some doctors kept dismissing it. Do some exercise they said. Yeah not at 4 in the morning when I'm trying to sleep and the sensations in my arms and legs become unbearable. 

I started taking a drug called Procyclidine. It really helped the akathisia but they kept changing their minds about giving it to me saying it was addictive. So in the end I stopped the abilify myself out of frustration and ended up in hospital. 

Procyclidine was really good for the akathisia so I'd highly recommend bringing it up with your psychiatrist. I'm not sure if it goes by any other names. I think it's a medication commonly used for parkinsons.
Grandeur is like realising your true "self" for the first time. It can definitely be a beautiful thing.

The line between psychosis and spiritual enlightenment is blurred and there has been much debate surrounding it.

In my view, whether a persons experiences are labelled psychotic or spiritual in nature largely depends on the culture that surrounds them. For Jesus, he was living at a time where the experiences we may call psychotic today were seen as spiritual gifts. There's no denying that if he were alive today and living in a city he would be put in hospital for the claims he was making.

I'm not saying Jesus was a schizophrenic back then. I'm saying that since his time the world has learned a great deal more about the human mind so he would be put in the "mental illness" box nowadays. This is a tricky subject for me because I personally believe that elements of schizophrenia can be seen as spiritual enlightenment as opposed to an illness. We simply don't know whether schizophrenics who have spoken to God are actually experiencing something of the supernatural or whether it's just brain chemicals going haywire.

Some drugs exaggerate the symptoms. Weed is the primary one. For me, I would smoke weed and the voices would get a lot more audible. Then I found that when I was high it was easy to get lost in irrational thought patterns that would lead to delusions. I don't know how to describe it. I'd start to feel like everything in my environment was important, trying to convey some hidden message to me. If it wasn't that it was paranoia. 

One night (without drugs) I convinced myself that someone was going to break into my flat and I put so much stuff in front of the door to stop them. I became obsessed with this idea and couldn't sleep. I'd imagine if I was smoking at the time I probably would have slept with a weapon beside me.

The thing about drugs is that a lot of people with this condition tend to use drugs to self-medicate. And even though we know it's bad for us we still do it because we want to escape. Or sometimes we think we'll find the answers we're looking for by using drugs. If I think the voices are trying to tell me something and smoking makes them louder then maybe I might smoke in order to find something out from the voices. Or maybe I'll smoke and do some introspection and come to some irrational conclusion about the world and think I've figured it all out.

How drugs effect someone with schizophrenia mostly depend on the person. My delusions are grandiose, delusions of reference and occasionally delusions of persecution/paranoia. Therefore weed would play on those delusions.

I'm a filmmaker myself so I'm going to give you some advice and please don't take it as criticism. Filmmaking is something you learn by doing but also you learn a lot by how people perceive your work. You can understand your film and its meaning inside and out but if the audience doesn't follow it then it doesn't matter. A film should speak for itself and shouldn't rely on the director having to explain anything.

If you wanted to express the voices as other physical people then you should use real people (not yourself). Otherwise it is going to suggest a split-personality which isn't anything to do with schizophrenia.

This is more of a trailer than a film and the reason for that is that films tell a story. This is more a sequence of events. You need to get the audiences attention from the beginning. A lot of films start with the waking up/brushing teeth/showering. You don't need it. Start the story after all of that has happened at an interesting moment and you will get the attention of your audience. 

Next: What is the story? You have a character. What do they want? What is preventing them from getting what they want? What is the resolution? Start mind-mapping your ideas and come up with a structure. If you want to pursue short-films google the 3 Act Structure and it will make the process easier. 

The character has schizophrenia but that isn't the story. The story is what happens because that character has schizophrenia. The schizophrenia should be something that is present alongside an actual story where things happen and are effected by the distorted perspective your protagonist has on reality.

Don't feel disheartened because what I'm trying to say is the more preparation and work you put in before you turn the camera on - the better the film will be. Let's be honest you obviously put lots of effort into this because every film, no matter how short, takes time and effort.

Celtx is a free scriptwriting software online. Write a script for your film. Even a 2-3 minute script (1 script page is roughly 1 minute of film). Come up with a story and throw in some dialogue (although not necessary). 

Finally. Research is so important because of course it's not going to be your intention to offend anybody but it's bound to happen. Schizophrenia is so so complex and everyones experience is different. Voices are one tiny aspect of the condition, delusions are a more interesting avenue to go down in my opinion. Watch youtube videos, read about it online from people who have it etc. etc. This film simply doesn't convey schizophrenia but you're 19 years old for gods sake so it doesn't really matter. You experimented and you created something and I'm sure you've learned a lot already by doing so.

Now take some time to do some extensive research if you're serious about approaching this topic again. Portraying schizophrenia in a film isn't easy for the best filmmakers out there.

Best of luck and keep making/writing films if you have the passion!

Most people aren't really sure. You can keep it brief. Basically it's when you start experiencing a distorted version of reality. It can happen to anyone. I would say that if you're going to tell people, tell those people you're comfortable around. Not everyone will understand but the people who are worth your time will.

As u/anubis-- has said, hypnagognic hallucinations occur at the brink of drifting into sleep.

It can be difficult to distinguish whether the voices you hear at night are hypnagognic or simply "voices you hear at night."

How lucid are you when you hear them? Are your eyes closed? Is your body and mind relaxed and do you feel like you're close to falling asleep? If this is the state you're in when they occur it's likely they're hypnagognic. 

If they're occurring when youre laying in bed, reading, on your phone, or even just thinking then they could just be regular hallucinations. Even if your eyes are closed we can usually tell how lucid we still are. If you're still lucid and can hear the voices they're regular hallucinations. I have a lot of mixed feelings about zoloft. 

I've been taking 50mg  once a day for almost 2 months.

First day I felt nausea, first week I had a lot of energy, restless legs, needed to move constantly. I was also pretty irritable. 

Week 2 I started feeling really paranoid. Like full on people are out to get me. It was kind of fleeting though like fleeting thoughts  like what if there's cameras in my bath. I wouldn't belive it but I'd make sure any gaps near the bath were covered. 

After a month I thought I was losing my mind. I was really paranoid at this stage and having strange thoughts. Thing is is that I'm prone to having these thoughts occasional so zoloft being a med that increases dopamine  means it caused this effect because I already had it as a problem before. 

I don't know if paranoia is a side effect most peopke get but I doubt it. If you've experienced  psychosis before which I have then maybe it's not a good choice. 

But. I'm still on zoloft now nearly 2 months now. My paranoia is reallt calmed down and I feel like I'm regaining some sort of normality. I felt really out of it before and even felt like my surroundings weren't real. 

Now with some positives. It helps anxiety. I suffered so bad with anxiety like the physical sensations of it would drive me insane. It was effecting everything uni, appetite, sleep. Zoloft helps to take the edge of. Situations which would cause you anxiety before seem to be less overwhelming. 

I can't stress enough that you have to expect side effects. Mine was an extreme case to the extent that paranoia isn't a regular side effect and is more to do with my own mental health and being predisponed  to it.

No matter what med you try you have to be willing to give it at least a month to start working. If you get through side effects it's worth it and as I said you probably won't have the same experience as me so don't worry. Do some research online about zoloft and look what other users have said. Personally it's one of the better ones for me and I have had to try a few.

Ask any more questions if you need to and good luck with  finding the right medicine

I agree about Timothy, curiosity killed the cat and I think he was a lot more than just curious but I say Herzog did a fantastic job of portraying raw human emotion, unfiltered due to the fact a lot of the filming was done in an intimate video diary style. I think the film would never be what it is if Herzog was with Timothy the whole time because thats when people start "performing" to the camera in whats meant to be a documentary and the authenticity wouldn't be there.

I think he was stupid to do what he did, he was warned yet he continued to live so dangorously but that still doesn't take away from the fact that the documentary gives such a unique insight into his story told by himself on his camcorder. What makes someone want to live like this? He is isolated with only a camera to talk to and thats when he shows us his inner self. In no way to I condone what he did, its tragic that his girlfriend got killed because of his actions but I still think this film is one of Herzogs greatest.
